Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In a directed graph with |V| vertices implemented via an adjacency list, the cost of processing a vertex v is determined by its out-degree, that is, the number of edges leaving v. The worst-case scenario and the aggregate amortized analysis both depend on how the edges are distributed among the vertices.

* The worst possible single operation cost is **|V| − 1**, which occurs when a single vertex has an outgoing edge to every other vertex in the graph, thereby maximizing its out-degree (assuming a simple directed graph with no self-loops or multi-edges).
* The average amortized cost, computed via aggregate analysis, is **|E| / |V|**, because the total cost over all |V| operations equals the sum of the out-degrees of all vertices, which is exactly |E| (the total number of edges in the graph), and dividing by the number of operations |V| yields the average.
